title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 14. Sri Jiyada-Nrisimha
html:
The Lord travels south: at Alalanatha He awakens love for Krishna in the people He embraces on the way; at Kurma-kshetra He heals the leper brahmana Vasudeva; at Jiyada-Nrisimha He tells the ancient story of that Deity

Verse 1

सार्वभौमभट्टाचार्यः स उद्विग्नो ह्यचेतनः।
एवं भक्तास्तदैवासन्सर्व उद्विग्नमानसाः॥१॥

sārvabhaumabhaṭṭācāryaḥ sa udvigno hyacetanaḥ|
evaṁ bhaktāstadaivāsansarva udvignamānasāḥ||1||

sarvabhauma-bhattacharyah — Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya; sah — he; udvignah — distressed; hi — indeed; achetanah — as if senseless; evam — so; bhaktah — the devotees; tada — then; eva — indeed; asan — were; sarve — all; udvigna-manasah — troubled at heart.

1Meanwhile Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya12 was so distressed that he was as if senseless; and so too all the devotees were troubled at heart at that time.

Verse 2

ततः श्रीकृष्णचैतन्यश्चलितो दक्षिणां दिशम्।
आलालनाथमागत्य प्रेमाद्देहमधैर्यतः॥२॥

tataḥ śrīkṛṣṇacaitanyaścalito dakṣiṇāṁ diśam|
ālālanāthamāgatya premāddehamadhairyataḥ||2||

tatah — then; shri-krishna-chaitanyah — Sri Krishna Chaitanya; chalitah — setting out; dakshinam — southern; disham — toward the direction; alalanatham — to Alalanatha; agatya — coming; premat — from love; deham — the body; adhairyatah — through loss of composure.

2Sri Krishna Chaitanya, for His part, set out southward and, coming to Alalanatha3, lost all control of His body for love:

Verse 3

कृष्ण कृष्णेति कृष्णेति उवाचोच्चैर्मुहुर्मुहुः।
क्षणं विलुठते भूमौ क्षणं मूर्च्छति जल्पति॥३॥

kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti kṛṣṇeti uvācoccairmuhurmuhuḥ|
kṣaṇaṁ viluṭhate bhūmau kṣaṇaṁ mūrcchati jalpati||3||

krishna krishna-iti krishna-iti — "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna!"; uvacha — cried; uchchaih — loudly; muhuh muhuh — again and again; kshanam — now; viluthate — rolls; bhumau — on the ground; kshanam — now; murchchhati — swoons; jalpati — babbles.

3loudly, again and again, He cried, "Krishna, Krishna, Krishna!" — now rolling on the ground, now swooning, now babbling,

Verse 4

क्षणं गायति गोविन्दकृष्णरामेति नामभिः।
महाप्रेमप्लुतं गात्रमालालनाथदर्शने॥४॥

kṣaṇaṁ gāyati govindakṛṣṇarāmeti nāmabhiḥ|
mahāpremaplutaṁ gātramālālanāthadarśane||4||

kshanam — now; gayati — sings; govinda-krishna-rama-iti — "Govinda, Krishna, Rama!"; namabhih — with the names; maha-prema-plutam — flooded with great love; gatram — His body; alalanatha-darshane — at the sight of Alalanatha.

4now singing the names "Govinda, Krishna, Rama!" — and at the sight of Alalanatha His whole body was flooded with great love.

Verse 5

कञ्चित्पथि जनं दृष्टमालिङ्गच्छक्तिसञ्चरैः।
स तत्र प्रेमविवशो नृत्यन्गायन्मुदैव च॥५॥

kañcitpathi janaṁ dṛṣṭamāliṅgacchaktisañcaraiḥ|
sa tatra premavivaśo nṛtyangāyanmudaiva ca||5||

kanchit — a certain; pathi — on the road; janam — man; drishtam — met; alingat — embraced; shakti-sancharaih — with infusions of power; sah — he; tatra — there; prema-vivashah — overwhelmed by love; nrityan — dancing; gayan — singing; muda — joyfully; eva — indeed; cha — and.

5Meeting a man on the road, He embraced him and passed His power into him; and the man, overwhelmed by love, at once began to dance and sing for joy.

Verse 6

निजगेहं जगाम स प्रेमधाराशतप्लुतः।
अन्यग्रामजनान्दृष्ट्वा प्रेमालिङ्गमकारयत्॥६॥

nijagehaṁ jagāma sa premadhārāśataplutaḥ|
anyagrāmajanāndṛṣṭvā premāliṅgamakārayat||6||

nija-geham — to his own home; jagama — went; sah — he; prema-dhara-shata-plutah — bathed in a hundred streams of love; anya-grama-janan — the people of other villages; drishtva — seeing; prema-alingam — a loving embrace; akarayat — gave.

6Bathed in a hundred streams of love, that man went home, and whenever he met the people of other villages he embraced them with love.

Verse 7

ते पुनः प्रेमविश्रान्तं गायन्ति च रमन्ति च।
एवं परम्परा येषु तान्सर्वान्समकारयत्॥७॥

te punaḥ premaviśrāntaṁ gāyanti ca ramanti ca|
evaṁ paramparā yeṣu tānsarvānsamakārayat||7||

te — they; punah — in turn; prema-vishrantam — resting in love; gayanti — sing; cha — and; ramanti — rejoice; cha — and; evam — thus; parampara — in succession; yeshu — among whom; tan — them; sarvan — all; samakarayat — made (so).

7And they in turn, at rest in love, sang and rejoiced. Thus, from one to another, He made them all alike.

Verse 8

आलालनाथक्षेत्रे स रात्रैकं संन्यवासयत्।
ततः परदिवोत्थाय प्रातःकार्यं समापयत्॥८॥

ālālanāthakṣetre sa rātraikaṁ saṁnyavāsayat|
tataḥ paradivotthāya prātaḥkāryaṁ samāpayat||8||

alalanatha-kshetre — in the land of Alalanatha; sah — He; ratra-ekam — one night; samnyavasayat — spent; tatah — then; para-dive — on the next day; utthaya — rising; pratah-karyam — the morning duties; samapayat — completed.

8He spent one night in the land of Alalanatha, and on the next day He rose, completed His morning duties,

Verse 9

प्रचलन्दक्षिणदेशमुवाच इति नृत्यति॥९॥

pracalandakṣiṇadeśamuvāca iti nṛtyati||9||

prachalan — setting out; dakshina-desham — for the southern country; uvacha — said; iti — thus; nrityati — dances.

9and, setting out for the southern country, sang thus and danced:

Verse 10

कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण हे।
कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण हे॥१०॥

kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa he|
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa he||10||

krishna — O Krishna (seven times); he — O!; krishna — O Krishna (seven times); he — O!

10"Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, O! Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, O!

Verse 11

कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण रक्ष माम्।
कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण पाहि माम्॥११॥

kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa rakṣa mām|
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa pāhi mām||11||

krishna — O Krishna (six times); raksha — save; mam — me; krishna — O Krishna (six times); pahi — protect; mam — me.

11Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, save me! Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, Krishna, protect me!"4

Verse 12

इति पठति स मन्त्रं प्रेमविप्लाविताश्रु-
र्लुठति धरणिमध्ये धावति च प्रकम्पैः।
इह हरिरिति वाक्यैर्बाष्परुद्धावकण्ठो
रुदति तरुलतायां प्रेमदृष्टिं करोति॥१२॥

iti paṭhati sa mantraṁ premaviplāvitāśru-
rluṭhati dharaṇimadhye dhāvati ca prakampaiḥ|
iha haririti vākyairbāṣparuddhāvakaṇṭho
rudati tarulatāyāṁ premadṛṣṭiṁ karoti||12||

iti — thus; pathati — recites; sah — He; mantram — the mantra; prema-viplavita-ashruh — His tears flooding with love; luthati — rolls; dharani-madhye — on the ground; dhavati — runs; cha — and; prakampaih — trembling; iha — here; harih — Hari; iti — (saying) thus; vakyaih — with words; bashpa-ruddha-ava-kanthah — His throat choked with tears; rudati — weeps; taru-latayam — on trees and creepers; prema-drishtim — a loving gaze; karoti — casts.

12Reciting this mantra, He was flooded with tears of love; He rolled on the ground and ran, shaken with trembling; saying, "Here is Hari!" He wept, His voice choked with tears, and cast loving glances at the trees and creepers.

Verse 13

आगते कूर्मक्षेत्रे च कूर्मरूपी जनार्दनः।
कूर्मनामा च विप्रेन्द्रो गतः सत्कृतिकर्मणि॥१३॥

āgate kūrmakṣetre ca kūrmarūpī janārdanaḥ|
kūrmanāmā ca viprendro gataḥ satkṛtikarmaṇi||13||

agate — when (He) had come; kurma-kshetre — to Kurma-kshetra; cha — and; kurma-rupi — in the form of the Tortoise; janardanah — Janardana; kurma-nama — named Kurma; cha — and; vipra-indrah — the best of brahmanas; gatah — set about; satkriti-karmani — the work of honouring (Him).

13When He came to Kurma-kshetra, where Janardana dwells in the form of the Tortoise, the best of brahmanas, named Kurma, set about honouring Him

Verse 14

भोजयञ्छ्रद्धया स्वन्नं प्रसादं कूर्म ईश्वरम्॥१४॥

bhojayañchraddhayā svannaṁ prasādaṁ kūrma īśvaram||14||

bhojayan — feeding; shraddhaya — with faith; su-annam — fine food; prasadam — prasada; kurmah — Kurma; ishvaram — the Lord.

14and with faith fed the Lord on fine food — prasada5.

Verse 15

ततो जगाम भगवाँल्लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया।
कूर्मक्षेत्रे जगन्नाथं ददर्श कूर्मरूपिणम्॥१५॥

tato jagāma bhagavā~llokānugrahakāmyayā|
kūrmakṣetre jagannāthaṁ dadarśa kūrmarūpiṇam||15||

tatah — then; jagama — went; bhagavan — Bhagavan; loka-anugraha-kamyaya — wishing to show grace to the people; kurma-kshetre — at Kurma-kshetra; jagannatham — Jagannatha; dadarsha — beheld; kurma-rupinam — in the form of the Tortoise.

15Then Bhagavan, wishing to show grace to the people, set out and at Kurma-kshetra6 beheld Jagannatha in the form of the Tortoise.

Verse 16

कूर्मनामा द्विजः कश्चित्तद्दर्शनमहोत्सवः।
आतिथ्यं विदधे हर्षान्मानयन्सफलं दिनम्॥१६॥

kūrmanāmā dvijaḥ kaścittaddarśanamahotsavaḥ|
ātithyaṁ vidadhe harṣānmānayansaphalaṁ dinam||16||

kurma-nama — named Kurma; dvijah — a brahmana; kashchit — a certain; tat-darshana-maha-utsavah — for whom seeing Him was a great festival; atithyam — hospitality; vidadhe — offered; harshat — out of joy; manayan — deeming; sa-phalam — fruitful; dinam — the day.

16A certain brahmana named Kurma, for whom the sight of the Lord was a great festival, joyfully offered Him hospitality and counted that day well spent.

Verse 17

वासुदेवो द्विजश्रेष्ठो दृष्ट्वा श्रीपुरुषोत्तमम्।
तद्दर्शनसमुल्लासैः कृष्णं ज्ञात्वा ननर्त च॥१७॥

vāsudevo dvijaśreṣṭho dṛṣṭvā śrīpuruṣottamam|
taddarśanasamullāsaiḥ kṛṣṇaṁ jñātvā nanarta ca||17||

vasudevah — Vasudeva; dvija-shreshthah — the best of brahmanas; drishtva — seeing; shri-purushottamam — Sri Purushottama; tat-darshana-samullasaih — with the rapture of beholding Him; krishnam — as Krishna; jnatva — recognising; nanarta — danced; cha — and.

17And Vasudeva7, the best of brahmanas, seeing Sri Purushottama, recognised Him as Krishna in the rapture of that sight and began to dance.

Verse 18

तं कुष्ठरोगिणं विप्रं महाभागवतोत्तमम्।
आलिङ्ग्य भगवांश्चक्रे स्वर्णकान्तिसमप्रभम्॥१८॥

taṁ kuṣṭharogiṇaṁ vipraṁ mahābhāgavatottamam|
āliṅgya bhagavāṁścakre svarṇakāntisamaprabham||18||

tam — that; kushtha-roginam — leprous; vipram — brahmana; maha-bhagavata-uttamam — the best of great devotees; alingya — embracing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; chakre — made; svarna-kanti-sama-prabham — shining with the lustre of gold.

18Bhagavan embraced that brahmana, a leper and the best of great devotees, and he shone like gold.

Verse 19

तौ दृष्ट्वा प्रेमसम्पूर्णौ स्वभक्तौ प्राह श्रीपतिः।
मदाज्ञया कृष्णभक्तिं लोकान्ग्राहयतां सुखम्॥१९॥

tau dṛṣṭvā premasampūrṇau svabhaktau prāha śrīpatiḥ|
madājñayā kṛṣṇabhaktiṁ lokāngrāhayatāṁ sukham||19||

tau — the two; drishtva — seeing; prema-sampurnau — filled with love; sva-bhaktau — His devotees; praha — said; shri-patih — the Husband of Shri; mat-ajnaya — by My command; krishna-bhaktim — devotion to Krishna; lokan — the people; grahayatam — may you two lead to accept; sukham — happily.

19Seeing both His devotees filled with love, the Husband of Shri said to them, "By My command lead the people to devotion to Krishna — easily and joyfully."

Verse 20

एवमुक्त्वा गौरचन्द्रस्तथैवान्तर्दधे हरिः।
विस्मापयन्स्वलोकान्कृष्णकृष्णेति कीर्तयन्॥२०॥

evamuktvā gauracandrastathaivāntardadhe hariḥ|
vismāpayansvalokānkṛṣṇakṛṣṇeti kīrtayan||20||

evam — thus; uktva — saying; gaura-chandrah — Gaurachandra; tatha eva — at once; antardadhe — vanished; harih — Hari; vismapayan — astonishing; sva-lokan — His people; krishna-krishna-iti — "Krishna, Krishna!"; kirtayan — chanting.

20So saying, Hari Gaurachandra at once vanished, chanting "Krishna, Krishna!" and leaving His people in amazement.

Verse 21

कियद्दूरं समागत्य जियडाख्यं नृसिंहकम्।
ददर्श परमप्रीतः प्रेमाश्रुपुलकाञ्चितः॥२१॥

kiyaddūraṁ samāgatya jiyaḍākhyaṁ nṛsiṁhakam|
dadarśa paramaprītaḥ premāśrupulakāñcitaḥ||21||

kiyad-duram — some distance; samagatya — having come; jiyada-akhyam — called Jiyada; nrisimhakam — Nrisimha; dadarsha — beheld; parama-pritah — overjoyed; prema-ashru-pulaka-anchitah — adorned with tears of love and thrilling hair.

21Going on a little further, He beheld with great delight the Nrisimha called Jiyada8; His eyes filled with tears of love and the hair of His body stood on end.

Verse 22

तस्य स्वभक्ताधीनत्वकथां प्राह पुरातनीम्।
स एव जगतां नाथः स्वयं भक्तजनप्रियः॥२२॥

tasya svabhaktādhīnatvakathāṁ prāha purātanīm|
sa eva jagatāṁ nāthaḥ svayaṁ bhaktajanapriyaḥ||22||

tasya — His (Nrisimha's); sva-bhakta-adhinatva-katham — the story of His subjection to His devotee; praha — told; puratanim — ancient; sah — He; eva — Himself; jagatam — of the worlds; nathah — the Lord; svayam — Himself; bhakta-jana-priyah — dear to His devotees.

22And the Lord of the worlds Himself, dear to His devotees, told the ancient story of how this Nrisimha submitted to His devotee:

Verse 23

अत्रैवासीत्पुरा कश्चित्पुण्डयेति समाख्यया।
कृषीवलो हि विख्यातो मायाम्बुफलमर्जयेत्॥२३॥

atraivāsītpurā kaścitpuṇḍayeti samākhyayā|
kṛṣīvalo hi vikhyāto māyāmbuphalamarjayet||23||

atra — here; eva — indeed; asit — there lived; pura — once; kashchit — a certain; pundaya-iti — Pundaya; samakhyaya — by name; krishivalah — a farmer; hi — indeed; vikhyatah — well known; mayambu-phalam — the mayambu fruit; arjayet — grew.

23"Once there lived here a farmer named Pundaya, known for growing mayambu fruit9.

Verse 24

वराहरूपिणा खण्डं विखण्डं कृतिना समम्।
युयोध बलवान्गोपः कृतपुण्यो मुरारिणा॥२४॥

varāharūpiṇā khaṇḍaṁ vikhaṇḍaṁ kṛtinā samam|
yuyodha balavāngopaḥ kṛtapuṇyo murāriṇā||24||

varaha-rupina — who had taken the form of a boar; khandam vikhandam — into bits and pieces; kritina — who had torn (the field); samam — with; yuyodha — fought; balavan — the strong; gopah — cowherd; krita-punyah — virtuous; murarina — with Murari.

24Murari, taking the form of a boar, tore his field to pieces, and the strong and virtuous cowherd fought with Him.

Verse 25

बाणविद्धेन तेनापि रामरामेति कीर्तनात्।
ज्ञातोऽसावीश्वर इति चोपवासादिमाचरत्॥२५॥

bāṇaviddhena tenāpi rāmarāmeti kīrtanāt|
jñāto'sāvīśvara iti copavāsādimācarat||25||

bana-viddhena — pierced by the arrow; tena — by Him (the Boar); api — indeed; rama-rama-iti — "Rama, Rama!"; kirtanat — from the crying out; jnatah — was recognised; asau — He; ishvarah — the Lord; iti — as; cha — and; upavasa-adim — fasting and the like; acharat — practised.

25But the Boar, pierced by his arrow, began to cry out, 'Rama, Rama!' — and from this the cowherd knew that He was the Lord, and he began to fast and keep other vows.

Verse 26

दयालुर्भगवानाह दुग्धसेकेन सर्वथा।
दर्शनं मे प्राप्स्यसि त्वं राज्ञा सह तथा वचः॥२६॥

dayālurbhagavānāha dugdhasekena sarvathā|
darśanaṁ me prāpsyasi tvaṁ rājñā saha tathā vacaḥ||26||

dayaluh — the merciful; bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; dugdha-sekena — by sprinkling milk; sarvatha — surely; darshanam — the sight; me — of Me; prapsyasi — will obtain; tvam — you; rajna — the king; saha — with; tatha — such; vachah — was the word.

26And the merciful Bhagavan said, 'Sprinkle this place with milk, and you will surely see Me together with the king.' Such was His word.

Verse 27

श्रुत्वा भगवतो वाक्यं गोपः प्रेमपरिप्लुतः।
आज्ञामावेदयत्सोऽपि तदाज्ञां च तथाकरोत्॥२७॥

śrutvā bhagavato vākyaṁ gopaḥ premapariplutaḥ|
ājñāmāvedayatso'pi tadājñāṁ ca tathākarot||27||

shrutva — hearing; bhagavatah — of Bhagavan; vakyam — the word; gopah — the cowherd; prema-pariplutah — overflowing with love; ajnam — the command; avedayat — made known; sah — he (the king); api — too; tat-ajnam — that command; cha — and; tatha — accordingly; akarot — carried out.

27Hearing the word of Bhagavan, the cowherd, overflowing with love, made the command known to the king, and the king carried it out exactly.

Verse 28

दुग्धसेचनमात्रेण भगवान्स्वमदर्शयत्।
श्रीविग्रहं सज्जनं च निवारणं यथाकरोत्॥२८॥

dugdhasecanamātreṇa bhagavānsvamadarśayat|
śrīvigrahaṁ sajjanaṁ ca nivāraṇaṁ yathākarot||28||

dugdha-sechana-matrena — merely by the pouring of milk; bhagavan — Bhagavan; svam — Himself; adarshayat — revealed; shri-vigraham — His holy form; sat-janam — to the virtuous; cha — and; nivaranam — the keeping away (of others); yatha — as; akarot — He did.

28Merely by the pouring of milk Bhagavan revealed Himself — His holy form — to the virtuous, and, as He did, kept the others away10.

Verse 29

कियत्कालावसानेन वार्तावित्तश्च कश्चन।
आगतो दर्शनार्थी स भार्यया समनुव्रतः॥२९॥

kiyatkālāvasānena vārtāvittaśca kaścana|
āgato darśanārthī sa bhāryayā samanuvrataḥ||29||

kiyat-kala-avasanena — after some time had passed; varta-vittah — one who lived by trade; cha — and; kashchana — a certain; agatah — came; darshana-arthi — wishing for darshan; sah — he; bharyaya — by his wife; samanuvratah — accompanied.

29Some time later a man who lived by trade came, accompanied by his wife, wishing to behold the Lord.

Verse 30

दर्शनानन्दमत्तः श्रीमन्दिरं तं प्रविष्टवान्।
प्राप्ते श्रीचरणाम्भोजे दृष्ट्वा हर्षमुपागतः॥३०॥

darśanānandamattaḥ śrīmandiraṁ taṁ praviṣṭavān|
prāpte śrīcaraṇāmbhoje dṛṣṭvā harṣamupāgataḥ||30||

darshana-ananda-mattah — intoxicated with the bliss of darshan; shri-mandiram — the holy temple; tam — that; pravishtavan — entered; prapte — attained; shri-charana-ambhoje — the holy lotus feet; drishtva — seeing; harsham — joy; upagatah — was filled with.

30Intoxicated with the bliss of that sight, he entered the holy temple, and on reaching and beholding the holy lotus feet he was filled with joy.

Verse 31

भगवानाह तं साधुमभीप्सितवरं वृणु।
जियडेति हि मे नाम गृहाण जगदीश्वर॥३१॥

bhagavānāha taṁ sādhumabhīpsitavaraṁ vṛṇu|
jiyaḍeti hi me nāma gṛhāṇa jagadīśvara||31||

bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; tam — to that; sadhum — good man; abhipsita-varam — the boon you desire; vrinu — choose; jiyada-iti — "Jiyada"; hi — indeed; me — my; nama — name; grihana — take; jagat-ishvara — O Lord of the world.

31Bhagavan said to that good man, 'Choose the boon you desire.' — 'My name is Jiyada: take that name, O Lord of the world!'

Verse 32

ओमित्याह जगद्योनिस्तेन च ख्यापितोऽभवत्।
श्रीजियडनृसिंहश्च भक्तवश्यो हरिः सदा॥३२॥

omityāha jagadyonistena ca khyāpito'bhavat|
śrījiyaḍanṛsiṁhaśca bhaktavaśyo hariḥ sadā||32||

om — "So be it"; iti — thus; aha — said; jagat-yonih — the Source of the world; tena — therefore; cha — and; khyapitah — renowned; abhavat — became; shri-jiyada-nrisimhah — as Sri Jiyada-Nrisimha; cha — and; bhakta-vashyah — submissive to His devotees; harih — Hari; sada — always.

32The Source of the world said, 'So be it,' and from then on He became renowned as Sri Jiyada-Nrisimha. For Hari is ever submissive to His devotees."

Verse 33

एतदाख्यद्धरिः साक्षाच्छ्रीगौराङ्गो महाप्रभुः।
अन्तर्दधे हि तत्रैव केन दृष्टः किल स्वयम्॥३३॥

etadākhyaddhariḥ sākṣācchrīgaurāṅgo mahāprabhuḥ|
antardadhe hi tatraiva kena dṛṣṭaḥ kila svayam||33||

etat — this; akhyat — told; harih — Hari; sakshat — in person; shri-gaurangah — Sri Gauranga; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu; antardadhe — vanished; hi — indeed; tatra — there; eva — right; kena — by whom; drishtah — was seen; kila — indeed; svayam — Himself.

33Having told this, Hari Himself, Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu, vanished from there — and who saw Him go?

Thus ends the fourteenth sarga, "The Story of Sri Jiyada-Nrisimha" (Shri-jiyada-nrisimha-prasanga), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. These and the following events take place after the Lord's departure from Puri (end of sarga 13).
  2. The verses of this sarga are given in the order of the Bengali edition (Calcutta, 1945): in this order the narrative follows the Lord's route (Alalanatha — Kurma-kshetra — Jiyada-Nrisimha) without a break. In the principal edition (Haridasa Shastri) verses 1–14 of this sarga stand as 14–27 and verses 15–27 as 1–13, so that the story of Jiyada is broken there; verses 28–33 are the same.
  3. Alalanatha: a temple of Vishnu at Brahmagiri, south of Puri.
  4. This prayer is also quoted in Krishnadasa Kaviraja's "Chaitanya Charitamrita" (Madhya 7.96).
  5. Verses 13–14 and 15–16 tell of the same event; v. 14, like v. 9, survives in all the editions only as a half-verse.
  6. Kurma-kshetra (Srikurmam): a shrine of Vishnu in the form of the Tortoise on the coast south of Orissa.
  7. Vasudeva: a brahmana suffering from leprosy, whom the Lord healed (v. 18).
  8. Jiyada-Nrisimha: the Deity of Nrisimha at Simhachala (near Vishakhapatnam); the origin of the name is told in vv. 29–32.
  9. The farmer's name and the name of the crop are obscure in the editions and are given as they read.
  10. The second half of the verse is obscure; the rendering is conjectural.
